title: The Great Fire of London — source-paced visual short

narration.voice_speed: clear, engaging and natural; not slow or overcompressed

reference_pacing: 63-66 second uploaded user examples; minimalist purposeful 3D movement, clear environmental geography
required_release_checks: every spoken clause has visible event or object within its exact shot
each beat has independently reviewed first/middle/end frames
no generic walls, fake historic landmarks or empty footage in place of named event
no audio dead air, clipped Qwen speech, wrong-timed foley, or speeding voices to fit
correct period clothing, building silhouettes, light and geography checked by human
all downloaded assets have verified commercial licenses and checksums
do not publish until user visually approves

asset_candidates.use: fire and smoke flipbooks (verify source manifest)

shots.spoken: In 1666, one ordinary bakery fire consumed much of medieval London.
shots.caption: ONE FIRE CHANGED LONDON
shots.required_visible_action: Start with the intact period city, then reveal the advancing blaze as a spatially connected area.

shots.spoken: Just after midnight, flames broke out at Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane.
shots.caption: PUDDING LANE • 2 SEPT
shots.required_visible_action: Embers at a baker's oven are shown as a possible ignition mechanism, not established fact; cut to smoke outside.

shots.spoken: The city was tinder-dry, with wooden houses leaning across its narrow lanes.
shots.caption: DRY TIMBER • NARROW LANES
shots.required_visible_action: Show upper wooden stories projecting almost together across the narrow street.

shots.spoken: A strong east wind carried sparks quickly from one roof to another.
shots.caption: WIND SPREAD THE FIRE
shots.required_visible_action: Track sparks moving consistently with the wind to ignite the next roof.
must_show: smoke drifting in same wind direction

shots.spoken: At the river, warehouses held oil, rope and other highly flammable goods.
shots.caption: DANGEROUS RIVER WAREHOUSES
shots.required_visible_action: Move camera from Thames waterside to period warehouse where rope, oil and timber intensify fire.

shots.spoken: Londoners rushed with leather buckets, but they had no organized fire brigade.
shots.caption: BUCKETS WERE NOT ENOUGH
shots.required_visible_action: Display a bucket relay pouring water on one burning facade; do not use modern fire engines.

shots.spoken: Workers dragged houses down to create gaps, yet the flames kept advancing.
shots.caption: THEY PULLED HOUSES DOWN
shots.required_visible_action: Period workers use hooks and ropes to pull wooden structures down, leaving a visible gap.

shots.spoken: Families fled through crowded streets, while some carried their possessions onto boats.
shots.caption: FAMILIES FLEE TO THE THAMES
shots.required_visible_action: Follow refugees carrying bundles to boats while smoke hangs over the riverfront.

shots.spoken: Even the enormous medieval St Paul's Cathedral was swallowed by the blaze.
shots.caption: OLD ST PAUL'S BURNS
shots.required_visible_action: Show a large medieval Gothic cathedral with long nave and period-appropriate roof catching fire; never modern dome.

shots.spoken: Only after the wind eased and buildings were demolished did the fire stop.
shots.caption: HOW THEY STOPPED IT
shots.required_visible_action: Show reduced wind and cleared firebreaks stopping the advancing fire. Mark the simplified diagram as reconstruction.

shots.spoken: Over four days, thirteen thousand two hundred houses and eighty-seven churches were destroyed.
shots.caption: 13,200 HOMES LOST
shots.required_visible_action: Reveal connected ruined streets and overlay historically supported totals without implying all houses visible.

shots.spoken: London rebuilt with stricter fire rules and more brick and stone buildings.
shots.caption: A CITY REBUILT
shots.required_visible_action: Match an original street angle to post-fire brick-and-stone reconstruction, showing the material change.
